title: Kirkwood council postpones vote on weekend noise ordinance hours
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Kirkwood council postpones vote on weekend noise ordinance hours
City staff had proposed shifting the weekend cutoff for noise limits from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays, but the council sent the issue back for more work rather than vote on it.
The Kirkwood City Council discussed proposed weekend time-of-day changes to a draft noise ordinance during an Oct. 1 work session but reached no vote, instead directing staff to continue revising the measure.
Darren, a city staff member, told the council the special business district had asked for later weekend hours. "I think that they were asking for 11:00 on Friday, Saturday um rather than 10 p.m. which was the change that was suggested at the last month's meeting um by the police department," he said.
DEBATE OVER MEASUREMENT Much of the discussion focused on whether decibel limits should be measured at the emitting property or the receiving property, a question tied to the broader ordinance rather than the weekend hours specifically. One council member argued enforcement should favor the receiving end, saying, "especially when you have business next to residential. You want to enforce the residential, don't we?"
CALLS FOR EXPERT INPUT A council member identified as Deb raised concerns that the ordinance lacked expert grounding. "I don't think we have an acoustical engineer on staff," she said, adding that updating the ordinance "needs a lot more scrutiny with experts to help us navigate it."
Another member pushed back on the pace of deliberation. "I think we're overkilling this thing personally right now," he said, arguing the council should focus on an immediate noise complaint rather than rewriting the whole code.
NEXT STEPS The council discussed forming a subcommittee or holding a dedicated work session with an expert to work through the ordinance details, including the weekend time changes. Darren said he would email his list of recommended changes to start that process.
